title: glasshouse submission manifest
description: What produced a benchmark number. Modelled on a manifest that was already being used to publish a real run, not designed from scratch: every field here exists because leaving it out made a published score impossible to reproduce.

source.description: paper, arXiv id, or repository the dataset and script came from

revision.description: commit or release of that source. Two people running 'the same benchmark' a year apart are often not.

hosted.description: true if the run went to a service the submitter operates. A hosted system cannot be re-run by a reader, which is a fact about the result, not a disqualification.

build.description: commit or artefact hash, when there is one

corpus.description: What was ingested. Two runs of the same benchmark can differ here.

ingest_failures.description: Report it even when it is zero, so a reader knows it was counted.

reader.description: The model that answers from what the memory system returned. A score belongs to the pair, never to the memory system alone.

via.description: how it was invoked, e.g. an API, a CLI

prompt.description: verbatim, or a path to it in this submission. Not a description.

note.description: if the benchmark does not specify a judge, say that here and say what you chose

prompts.description: Verbatim text or paths to it. A described prompt is not a published prompt.

query_transform.description: anything applied to the question before retrieval

aggregation.description: how per-question grades become the headline number

not_implemented.description: parts of the benchmark's own scoring you did not run. Saying so is normal and is what makes two numbers comparable.

runs.description: Every run, not the best one. A mean has to show what it is a mean of.

errors.description: questions that did not complete. A question that errored is not a question that was answered wrong, and the difference has to be visible.

headline.description: The single number you would put in a post, and how it comes from runs.

from.description: e.g. mean of runs r1, r2, r3

records.description: Path to the per-question record in this submission. Adding up what is there has to give the headline.

affiliation.description: who you work for. Used for the conflict-of-interest rule, not to weigh the result.
